plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 27: Direct-Current Circuits
plan.contextChunk: This figure places two drawings of the same circuit side by side, labeled (a) and (b) beneath them. Each is a rectangle split by a single vertical wire into two adjacent loops. Two blue zigzag resistor symbols sit along the top wire, labeled R1 = 3.00 ohms on the left and R3 = 3.00 ohms on the right. The dividing branch carries R2 = 3.00 ohms and the right-hand vertical wire carries R4 = 4.00 ohms, while the left-hand vertical wire is a plain conductor. Two battery symbols sit along the bottom: V1 = 24.00 V in the left loop, plus terminal on the left, and V2 = 29.00 V in the right loop, plus terminal on the right. Panel (b) repeats every element unchanged and adds six teal dots at the corners and branch points, lettered a, b, and c across the top and f, e, and d across the bottom. Setting the bare circuit beside the lettered copy separates the physical layout from the labels laid over it. The pair prepares a multi-loop network for analysis with Kirchhoff's junction and loop rules, the two points where three wires meet serving as the junctions.

interactionPlan.concept: Kirchhoff's junction and loop rules turn a two-loop circuit into a solvable set of equations: currents must balance at every junction, and signed potential changes must sum to zero around every closed path.
elements: Outer rectangle wire frame forming the circuit boundary
Single vertical middle wire dividing the rectangle into a left loop and a right loop
Blue zigzag resistor R1 = 3.00 Ω on the top-left wire segment
Blue zigzag resistor R3 = 3.00 Ω on the top-right wire segment
Blue zigzag resistor R2 = 3.00 Ω on the vertical middle branch
Blue zigzag resistor R4 = 4.00 Ω on the right vertical wire
Plain conducting left vertical wire (no component)
Battery symbol V1 = 24.00 V on the bottom-left wire, + terminal on the left, − on the right
Battery symbol V2 = 29.00 V on the bottom-right wire, − terminal on the left, + on the right
Teal node dots at six points: top-left, top-middle, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-middle, bottom-right
Italic node letters a (top-left), b (top-middle), c (top-right), f (bottom-left), e (bottom-middle), d (bottom-right)
Panel captions (a) unlabeled circuit and (b) lettered circuit
Current arrows I1 (left branch), I2 (middle branch), I3 (right branch) shown on demand
Junction equation callout box (e.g. I1 + I2 = I3)
Loop-rule accumulator panel listing signed terms as the traversal proceeds
Highlight glow used to mark the active branch, resistor, or battery

interactions.label: Circuit view
interactions.teaches: Node letters and dots are analysis scaffolding drawn onto an unchanged physical circuit, not new components.
At a junction where three branches meet, the currents entering equal the currents leaving, giving one independent equation per junction (b and e give the same equation).

interactions.label: Trace loop
interactions.teaches: Walking a closed path in a fixed direction assigns each element a sign — rise when entering the − terminal of a battery, drop when moving with the current through a resistor — and all signed terms must add to zero.

demo_steps.title: The bare circuit
demo_steps.narration: Two loops share a middle branch: R1 and R3 sit on top, R2 divides the loops, R4 is on the right, and two opposing batteries drive the bottom. Nothing here tells you where to start an analysis.

demo_steps.title: Add the labels
demo_steps.narration: Flip to panel (b): six teal dots and the letters a–f appear over the identical circuit. The physics is unchanged; the letters simply give you names for the points you will write equations about.

demo_steps.title: Find the junctions
demo_steps.narration: Only b and e have three wires meeting. Click either one to see its three branch currents; the junction rule says what flows in must flow out, so I1 + I2 = I3.

demo_steps.title: Start a loop
demo_steps.narration: Pick the left loop abef and choose a traversal direction. The accumulator panel opens empty, ready to collect signed potential changes.

demo_steps.title: Cross the battery
demo_steps.narration: Moving through V1 from − to + is a potential rise of +24.00 V. The term is added to the running sum and the battery glows.

demo_steps.title: Drop across R1
demo_steps.narration: Traversing R1 in the direction of I1 gives a drop of −I1(3.00 Ω). Sign comes entirely from the direction of travel relative to the assumed current.

demo_steps.title: Drop across R2
demo_steps.narration: Continuing down the shared middle branch through R2 adds −I2(3.00 Ω). The shared branch is what couples the two loops together.

demo_steps.title: Close the loop
demo_steps.narration: Returning along the plain left wire adds nothing. Back at the starting node, the potential must be what it was when you left.

demo_steps.title: The loop equation
demo_steps.narration: All terms sum to zero: 24.00 − 3.00 I1 − 3.00 I2 = 0. Repeat for the right loop and combine with the junction equation to solve for all three currents.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Labeling nodes is not decoration — it converts a picture of wires into a bookkeeping system where each junction gives a current equation and each closed loop gives a signed voltage equation, and together they pin down every unknown current.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Draw a wide horizontal rectangle of black wire with one vertical wire down the middle, splitting it into two equal square-ish loops. Two blue zigzag resistors on the top wire (R1 left, R3 right), one blue zigzag on the middle vertical branch (R2), one blue zigzag on the right vertical wire (R4); left vertical wire is a plain line. Bottom wire carries two multi-plate battery symbols: V1 in the left loop with + on its left side and − on its right, V2 in the right loop with − on its left and + on its right. Labels in serif italic math style: R1 = 3.00 Ω and R3 = 3.00 Ω above the top resistors, R2 = 3.00 Ω and R4 = 4.00 Ω to the left of their vertical resistors, V1 = 24.00 V and V2 = 29.00 V above their batteries. In the lettered view add filled teal dots at the six corner/branch points with italic letters a, b, c left-to-right along the top and f, e, d left-to-right along the bottom, letters placed just outside the frame. Use a warm highlight (orange/amber glow with thicker stroke) for the active branch or element during loop tracing, and a contrasting current-arrow color (e.g. red) for I1, I2, I3 arrows with small labels near mid-branch. Equation callouts appear in a light panel near the relevant junction or below the circuit, accumulating terms one line at a time. Caption '(a)' or '(b)' centered beneath the diagram matching the toggle state.

authoredContext:
Consider the circuit in the figure(a). Let us analyze this circuit to find the current through each resistor. First, label the circuit as shown in part (b).

(a) A multi-loop circuit. (b) Label the circuit to help with orientation.

Part a shows a circuit with two horizontal branches and three vertical branches. The first horizontal branch has two resistors of 3 Ω each and the second branch has two voltage sources of 24 V with positive terminal on the left and 29 V with positive terminal on the right. The left vertical branch is directly connected, the middle branch has a resistance of 3 Ω and the right branch has a resistance of 4 Ω. Part b shows the same circuit as part a with labelled junctions

Next, determine the junctions. In this circuit, points b and e each have three wires connected, making them junctions. Start to apply Kirchhoff’s junction rule (∑ Iin=∑ Iout) by drawing arrows representing the currents and labeling each arrow, as shown in the figure(b). Junction b shows that I1=I2+I3 and Junction e shows that I2+I3=I1. Since Junction e gives the same information of Junction b, it can be disregarded. This circuit has three unknowns, so we need three linearly independent equations to analyze it.

discrepancies: Source shows panels (a) and (b) side-by-side for direct comparison; the generated figure shows only one at a time behind a checkbox toggle (acceptable, but the at-a-glance two-panel composition of the source is lost).

Battery symbols are drawn with nearly uniform short plates at small scale; the source clearly alternates two long thin plates with two short thick plates, making the +/− convention more visually explicit.
Resistor zigzags are somewhat smaller/thinner relative to the wire rectangle than the bold blue zigzags in the source, slightly reducing the visual weight of the components.
Step-3 narration states the junction rule as 'I1 + I2 = I3' while the on-canvas callout and the node popup state 'I₁ = I₂ + I₃' for the same drawn arrow directions — an internal contradiction.

Extra explanatory panels (amber loop-rule accumulator, teal junction callout, red current arrows) appear over/below the circuit in later steps; these are additions not in the source (defensible pedagogically, but they change the look when active).
evaluation.notes: The default state is a close, clean replica of panel (a) with correct component values, layout and blue resistors, and the interaction set (9-step player, (a)/(b) toggle, loop-trace dropdown, junction rule, current arrows, hover/click detail) is unusually strong; main weaknesses are a self-contradictory junction-rule statement between narration and callout and slightly under-weighted battery/resistor symbols.
action_items: Make the junction-rule statement consistent: with I₂ drawn downward out of node b, every narration, tooltip and callout should read I₁ = I₂ + I₃ (fix the step-3 narration text).
Redraw the battery symbol with clearly alternating long-thin and short-thick plates (as in the source) and increase its overall size so the +/− terminals read at inline scale.
Slightly increase resistor zigzag amplitude/stroke weight so the blue components carry the same visual weight as in the source figure.
Consider showing the (b) node letters as a side-by-side second panel option (or a clear 'panel (a) / panel (b)' segmented button) so the toggle's role in reproducing the two-panel source is obvious.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are sound; remaining issues are concrete implementation fixes (contradictory step-3 narration text, battery/resistor symbol weight, panel toggle labeling).

Battery symbol V2 = 29.00 V on the bottom-right wire, − terminal on the left, + on the right
Teal node dots at six points: top-left, top-middle, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-middle, bottom-right
Italic node letters a (top-left), b (top-middle), c (top-right), f (bottom-left), e (bottom-middle), d (bottom-right)
Panel captions (a) unlabeled circuit and (b) lettered circuit
Current arrows I1 (left branch), I2 (middle branch), I3 (right branch) shown on demand

interactions.label: Circuit view
interactions.teaches: Node letters and dots are analysis scaffolding drawn onto an unchanged physical circuit, not new components.
At a junction where three branches meet, the currents entering equal the currents leaving, giving one independent equation per junction (b and e give the same equation).

interactions.label: Trace loop
interactions.teaches: Walking a closed path in a fixed direction assigns each element a sign — rise when entering the − terminal of a battery, drop when moving with the current through a resistor — and all signed terms must add to zero.

demo_steps.title: The bare circuit
demo_steps.narration: Two loops share a middle branch: R1 and R3 sit on top, R2 divides the loops, R4 is on the right, and two opposing batteries drive the bottom. Nothing here tells you where to start an analysis.

demo_steps.title: Add the labels
demo_steps.narration: Flip to panel (b): six teal dots and the letters a–f appear over the identical circuit. The physics is unchanged; the letters simply give you names for the points you will write equations about.

demo_steps.title: Find the junctions
demo_steps.narration: Only b and e have three wires meeting. Click either one to see its three branch currents; the junction rule says what flows in must flow out, so I1 + I2 = I3.

demo_steps.title: Start a loop
demo_steps.narration: Pick the left loop abef and choose a traversal direction. The accumulator panel opens empty, ready to collect signed potential changes.

demo_steps.title: Cross the battery
demo_steps.narration: Moving through V1 from − to + is a potential rise of +24.00 V. The term is added to the running sum and the battery glows.

demo_steps.title: Drop across R1
demo_steps.narration: Traversing R1 in the direction of I1 gives a drop of −I1(3.00 Ω). Sign comes entirely from the direction of travel relative to the assumed current.

demo_steps.title: Drop across R2
demo_steps.narration: Continuing down the shared middle branch through R2 adds −I2(3.00 Ω). The shared branch is what couples the two loops together.

demo_steps.title: Close the loop
demo_steps.narration: Returning along the plain left wire adds nothing. Back at the starting node, the potential must be what it was when you left.

demo_steps.title: The loop equation
demo_steps.narration: All terms sum to zero: 24.00 − 3.00 I1 − 3.00 I2 = 0. Repeat for the right loop and combine with the junction equation to solve for all three currents.

plan.keyInsight: Labeling nodes is not decoration — it converts a picture of wires into a bookkeeping system where each junction gives a current equation and each closed loop gives a signed voltage equation, and together they pin down every unknown current.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Draw a wide horizontal rectangle of black wire with one vertical wire down the middle, splitting it into two equal square-ish loops. Two blue zigzag resistors on the top wire (R1 left, R3 right), one blue zigzag on the middle vertical branch (R2), one blue zigzag on the right vertical wire (R4); left vertical wire is a plain line. Bottom wire carries two multi-plate battery symbols: V1 in the left loop with + on its left side and − on its right, V2 in the right loop with − on its left and + on its right. Labels in serif italic math style: R1 = 3.00 Ω and R3 = 3.00 Ω above the top resistors, R2 = 3.00 Ω and R4 = 4.00 Ω to the left of their vertical resistors, V1 = 24.00 V and V2 = 29.00 V above their batteries. In the lettered view add filled teal dots at the six corner/branch points with italic letters a, b, c left-to-right along the top and f, e, d left-to-right along the bottom, letters placed just outside the frame. Use a warm highlight (orange/amber glow with thicker stroke) for the active branch or element during loop tracing, and a contrasting current-arrow color (e.g. red) for I1, I2, I3 arrows with small labels near mid-branch. Equation callouts appear in a light panel near the relevant junction or below the circuit, accumulating terms one line at a time. Caption '(a)' or '(b)' centered beneath the diagram matching the toggle state.

discrepancies: In the default two-panel view the whole circuit is drawn at 0.58 scale and pushed into the upper-left of the canvas, leaving a large empty strip along the bottom (reserved for the later accumulator panel); the source fills its frame, so the step-0 state reads smaller and airier than the original.

Because of that 0.58 scale, every component label (R₁ = 3.00 Ω, V₁ = 24.00 V, node letters) renders at roughly 8–9 px — noticeably smaller and harder to read than the crisp serif labels in the source.
In panel (b) the node letter 'e' (y≈337 local) and the panel caption '(b)' (y≈352) are only ~15 px apart and visually crowd/overlap; the source separates them clearly.

Resistor zigzags use only 4 shallow peaks with rounded joins, whereas the source shows a taller, tighter multi-peak zigzag — the resistor glyph reads slightly flatter/less distinct, especially at overview scale.
Battery glyphs are drawn as four plates of alternating length; the source shows a longer multi-cell stack, so the batteries look a bit compressed relative to the wire segments they interrupt.
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful two-panel reproduction with correct resistor/battery/node topology and an excellent, conceptually correct Kirchhoff walkthrough (9 demo steps, loop-trace dropdown, current toggle, junction callout, hover/click detail); the main weaknesses are the shrunken default composition with dead space below and consequently undersized labels plus a crowded 'e'/'(b)' pair.
action_items: Scale the two-panel overview up (or reduce the reserved bottom strip until an overlay is active) so the step-0 state fills the frame like the source and labels render at readable size (≥12 px effective).
Move the panel captions '(a)'/'(b)' further down or offset node 'e' label so they no longer crowd each other in panel (b).
Increase the resistor zigzag peak count/amplitude and lengthen the battery cell stack so both glyphs match the source proportions more closely.
Consider keeping overview label font size constant (counter-scale text) instead of uniformly scaling the group, so panel text stays legible at inline size.
